column1: # One row per refutation IDENTITY of the verified survey (`targo trust check
# --allow-l0-gaps`, debug profile, trustc 321aaeda7). A refutation is a
# `failed` row OR a native CHC/PDR refutation the seal publishes as `unknown`
# (its verdict names `refuted obligation`: `refutation_route` in the script,
# the same text gate 13 counts); a row may be either. Identity: crate, source file,
# enclosing function (the report's path after its cargo-target prefix),
# obligation kind, and the source text the refuted span covers (whitespace
# collapsed, cut at 100 characters with `…`) — never a line number, so an
# unrelated edit does not move a row, and never an obligation id, which is not
# stable across identical runs. `--check-ledger` (gate 15's SKIP path) and the
# script tests hold every row's text to its file. Then `count`, the number of
# refuted rows the identity carries (several checks — null, validity,
# alignment — can share one span and kind): the ledger is a multiset, so a
# judged run with MORE rows at an identity fails and one with fewer reports the
# rest missing. Then its class and cause. For a
# JUDGED crate the gate FAILS on any refuted row whose identity is not here,
# and reports a row here whose refutation is absent as "expected refutation
# missing — NOT JUDGED for that row" (never a pass; never deleted by the tool).
# The one refutation class with no row here: a demoted `postcondition`
# refutation of a law of crates/trust-ir-laws/src/laws.rs, which gate 13 proves
# at --release and this debug survey admits on gate 13's verdict (`gate13_law`).
# class `verifier-false`: Trust's refutation is false. The cause names the shape
#   first (`shape a|b|c|d|e`, SHAPES in the script), then why the op cannot
#   fail. Shapes a, b, d and e, and shape c's `null reference constructed`
#   check of a Box deref (`Nest::width`), reproduce in
#   shape c's allocation and separation-logic checks prove in isolation and
#   are shown only by the rows themselves.
# class `policy`: a hardened-profile row trust-ir keeps by a recorded decision:
#   the cause begins `<decision> POLICY rows: ` for a decision of the script's
#   CLOSED table POLICY_DECISIONS (today d5db1e5d, stage 0), and the row's kind
#   must be one that decision covers (d5db1e5d: `unbounded_allocation` only).
# class `true` is FORBIDDEN (the gate refuses the ledger): a true refutation is
#   a defect to fix at its root.
# Remove a row when its refutation is gone. Rows are sorted by identity;
